speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You offered me an opinion on the stair. Now you will see what an opinion costs, and you will carry.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A side of bacon. I said four shillings, and I will say it once at the stall, so you can kill it properly.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Say it, then.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Four shillings for that side.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I will not write four shillings because you liked the sound. The price stays in my book.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: It is a side, sir, not a guess. Take the near corner.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have the corner.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Suet next. You will not name a sum. You will hold the basin while I point.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am holding it. I am not pricing it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The suet is hers to weigh. He can carry the basin.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: A firkin of salt. You will not tell me what a firkin costs. You will tell me whether the two of you can get it up the stair.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: She can lift it if I take the bottom. I do not know the price, and I am done pretending.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Good. That is the first true thing you have said in this market.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Onions on a string. They hang. They do not need his opinion.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They can hang. I will take the string if you put it in my hand.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: A cheese for the cold weeks. A cheese that will keep on a narrow stair, not a wheel you cannot turn on the landing.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I can turn a cheese. I cannot price one. You have had that from me at every stall.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: And I will have it at this one. You are useful carrying and no use at all at guessing. The household book is mine.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The quarter of beef is already in our tub, sir. Do not add it a second time in your head.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not add it. I pay nothing toward the stores. The firing is the sixpence. The candles are fourpence the pound, and they are mine, not these.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Fourpence the candles is your line, and you may keep it. The bacon is not your line. Give me your back as far as the close.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The back is yours as far as the close. My tables get one line, and not a price.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Then write the line at home. Do not write it on a stall where a man might think you meant it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: He may write that bacon is a mystery. He may not write what I paid.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Bacon is a mystery. I have not paid. I am carrying.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Carry, then. The colliers will still be in the close, and you can take a sack because it is there, not because you understand coal.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A sack I understand. A price I leave.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The string is cutting your hand, sir. Shift it. The cheese is the one that will want the landing.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Shifted. Lead.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Home. If you speak a number between here and the door, you can carry the firkin without help.
